the Nck adaptor protein is recruited to the TCR through a proline-rich motif in the cytoplasmic tail of CD3ε and that this recruitment is essential for the initiation of the TCR signaling cascade.
Nck recruitment is required for the full activation of T cells in vivo, as shown in two different experimental settings.

the Nck recruitment to TCR is fundamental in vivo for T cell activation, and that the interaction of NCK with CD3ε may represent a potential therapeutic target for pharmacological control of T cell activation.
